# Cetiyajātaka (Ja 422)

**Section:** Jātaka (ja)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cetiyajātaka* (Ja 422) is a canonical birth-story preserved in the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon. According to the narrative framework set at Jetavana, the Buddha relates the story after the monks discuss Devadatta sinking into the earth and falling into the Avīci hell on account of speaking falsely, remarking that this was not the first time Devadatta had been swallowed by the earth. In the story of the past, a monarch of ancient times—the king of Ceti—desires to elevate a younger brother above an elder one and utters a deliberate falsehood [Anandajoti 2010]. The commentary to the *Saṃyutta Nikāya* cites this figure as the perpetrator of the first lie of the present world aeon [Bodhi 2003]. Despite repeated admonitions from the Bodhisatta, who warns the king with verses declaring that injured truth (*dhamma*) inevitably harms the wrongdoer and causes the gods to depart, the king persists in his lie, loses his magical powers, and gradually sinks into the earth [Anandajoti 2010; Appleton 2010].

Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal alignment with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (37 matches) as well as grammatical citations in the *Saddanītippakaraṇaṃ* (*Padamālā*) [DharmaNexus]. In Tibetan translation, DharmaNexus detects cross-language matches with the *Jinamārgāvatāra* (D3964), Bhāviveka's *Madhyamakahṛdayavṛttitarkajvālā* (D3856), and Kṣemendra's *Bodhisatvāvadānakalpalatā* (D4155) [DharmaNexus].
